result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A's bars don't match its axis: November (112) and December (104) rise above the 120 gridline, and January (82) reads as about 105. A reader using the axis would get every value wrong. B's bars line up with its gridlines, it has a plain title with mm stated, and it uses a single color, labelling only the wettest and driest months. A's direct labels and teal highlight for Oct–Dec are nice, but they don't make up for an axis that misstates the data. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A's bars match its gridlines (Jan 82 sits near 90, Nov 112 just under 120), and it has a plain title, stated mm units, one restrained colour and direct labels on the wettest and driest months. B has a nicer light theme and highlights the wet season well, but its value axis doesn't match the data: Jan 82 reaches about 110 on the scale, and Oct 89 and Nov 112 rise above the 120 gridline. That misrepresents the values, even though the baseline is at zero. A's dark theme suits a printed newsletter less well, but its chart is accurate, which matters more.
